clips.title: The story
paras: The Etched Rune is a written summons delivered to novice dwarven hunters assisting the guard in Coldridge Valley. Passed on by Sten Stoutarm, the inscribed stone directs fledgling trackers to seek out Thorgas Grimson inside Anvilmar to formally begin their martial and wilderness training.

While helping Sten Stoutarm deal with nearby threats around Coldridge Valley, promising dwarven hunters are handed an inscribed stone tablet known as the Etched Rune. Rather than delivering spoken orders or simple parchment, dwarven mentors favor carved runes to impart formal missives. The rune instructs the recipient to take stock of their early work and present themselves indoors at Anvilmar for deeper instruction in the art of the hunt.

Presenting the rune to Thorgas Grimson marks a hunter's entry into formal discipline. Thorgas stresses that mountaineering and survival in Khaz Modan demand deep respect for the harsh environment: reading tracks in bitter snowdrifts, maintaining one's weapon and ammunition, and understanding the wild beasts that roam the crags. The etched stone serves as the hunter's first step from a lone wanderer with a gun into an apprentice of Anvilmar's veteran pathfinders.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: While you were helping me out, this rune was given to me to pass on to you. Take some time to read it when you have a chance. I'm thinkin' it came from the hunter trainer Thorgas. Take a gander at it and go find him inside Anvilmar when you've a chance.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Ya made it! Good to hear! Betcha didn't have to track me to find the place either. Haha!

Our profession is pretty steeped in tradition, friend. Learning the ways of the land. Learning to track a bear through the mountains. Even just surviving on wits alone takes a great deal of courage and cunning. Think you're capable?

clips.title: Completion
paras: One thing you should always remember is that you gotta respect the world you're livin' in. The beasts that choose to fight along side you; the shine of your weapon; the weight of your ammo; the bite of a bitter wind; all these things you need to know intimately.
I'll do what I can to help you, but most of the work's up to you. Anytime you think you're ready, come back and talk to me. I'll train you when I can.
